t: A Siamese kingdom on an island in the Chao Phraya that dominated the central plain of Thailand from 1351 to 1767.
Its wealth came from rice and royal trade, with Chinese, Japanese, Persian, Portuguese, Dutch and French merchants living in the capital.
Burma conquered it in 1569 and destroyed it in 1767, but its institutions passed to Thonburi and Bangkok.
dyk: In 1753 monks sent from Ayutthaya restored the full ordination of Buddhist monks in Sri Lanka, founding the Siyam Nikaya, still the island's largest order.
ev: U Thong founds Ayutthaya and reigns as Ramathibodi I
Ayutthaya absorbs the kingdom of Sukhothai
Bayinnaung of Burma takes Ayutthaya after a long siege
Naresuan defeats the Burmese at the Battle of Nong Sarai
The Siamese envoy Kosa Pan is received by Louis XIV at Versailles
Phetracha seizes power and expels the French garrison
Konbaung armies sack and burn Ayutthaya
